newsitem.title: USA: U.S. manufacturers' profits rose in Q3.
newsitem.headline: U.S. manufacturers' profits rose in Q3.

text.p: After-tax profits of U.S. manufacturing companies averaged a seasonally adjusted 6.6 cents per dollar of sales in the third quarter of 1996, the Commerce Department said Monday.
That was up from 6.2 cents per dollar of sales in the second quarter. It was also higher than profits in the third quarter of 1995, which averaged a seasonally adjusted 5.7 cents per dollar of sales.
Total seasonally adjusted profits after taxes were $62.6 billion on net sales of $944.2 billion in the third quarter.
In the second quarter, profits were $57.4 billion on net sales of $922.8 billion. In the third quarter of last year, profits were $50.1 billion on net sales of $884.6 billion.
The report is based on quarterly financial reports from about 7,800 corporations, the department said.
After-tax profits of non-durable manufacturing companies rose to $34.8 billion in the third quarter of 1996 from $31.9 billion in the second quarter.
After-tax profits of durables manufacturers rose to $27.8 billion in the third quarter from $25.6 billion in the second quarter, the department said.
